activity_context.topic_title: Double Integrals Over Type I Regions

feedback.problem: If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y=\frac{3}{2}-x$ and $y=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2},$ then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's make a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100085/assets/50a6b2d57fe4dbfbef58b49ae51b89f2001035fa896118eec1e3fcabcde626d9.png)

Now, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. 

- To determine the $x$-limits, we need to find the $x$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}-x & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2} \\ 3-2x & ={x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+2x-3 & =0 \\ (x+3)(x-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x$-limits are 
$-3\le x\le 1.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100085/assets/78e2ec78c9fb00fb56b7f84b2a5dbb96786dd07e3057b894ad2421e89ede29e2.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-3\le x\le 1,\,\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\le y\le \frac{3}{2}-x}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{-3}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}/2}^{3/2-x}f(x,y)\text{ }dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{1}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}/2}^{3/2-x}f(x,y)\text{ }dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$
